facts.fact_text: On 3 March 1999 the applicant and some seventy other persons took part in a picket in front of Komunenergiya's main office.
On 10 March 1999 the applicant was dismissed from work for systematic breach of her duties of employment pursuant to Article 40 § 3 of the Labour Code of 1971.
Article 44 of the Constitution of Ukraine provides that employees have the right to strike in order to protect their economic and social interests.

Article 44 of the Constitution of Ukraine provides that the procedure for exercising the right to strike shall be established by law, taking into account the need to ensure national security, the protection of health, and the rights and freedoms of other persons.
Article 44 of the Constitution of Ukraine provides that no one shall be forced to participate or to not participate in a strike.
Article 44 of the Constitution of Ukraine provides that a strike may only be prohibited on the basis of law.

Section 17 of the Resolution of Labour Disputes (Procedure) Act of 3 March 1998 defines a strike as a temporary, collective and voluntary cessation of work by employees with the aim of resolution of a collective labour dispute.

Section 17 of the Resolution of Labour Disputes (Procedure) Act of 3 March 1998 provides that striking shall be an extreme means of resolution of a collective labour dispute when all other possibilities of such resolution have been exhausted and the employer refuses to allow the claims of employees or of a body authorised by them, or of a trade union, or of an association of trade unions or of a body authorised by them.

Section 18 of the Resolution of Labour Disputes (Procedure) Act of 3 March 1998 provides that pursuant to Article 44 of the Constitution of Ukraine employees have the right to strike in order to protect their economic and social interests.

Section 27 of the Resolution of Labour Disputes (Procedure) Act of 3 March 1998 provides that employees' participation in a strike, with the exception of strikes declared unlawful by a court, shall not be considered as a violation of work discipline and may not serve as a ground for disciplinary action.

Section 28 of the Resolution of Labour Disputes (Procedure) Act of 3 March 1998 provides that organisation of, or participation in, a strike declared unlawful by a court shall constitute a violation of work discipline.
Section 28 of the Resolution of Labour Disputes (Procedure) Act of 3 March 1998 provides that employees shall not be remunerated for the time during which they take part in a strike.
